FormModule.Name: CUSTOMERS
FormModule.Title: Customer Maintenance
FormModule.Comment: Customer master maintenance: status gating, credit limit and duplicate-validation examples for the LOM modernization lab.

ModuleParameter.Name: P_CUSTOMER_ID
ModuleParameter.Comment: Optional: pre-filters the initial query when this form is opened from ORDERS.fmb (BT_VIEW_CUSTOMER, LOM-MOD-023).

Trigger.Name: WHEN-NEW-FORM-INSTANCE
Trigger.TriggerText:
BEGIN
 :GLOBAL.G_USER := NVL(:GLOBAL.G_USER, GET_APPLICATION_PROPERTY(USERNAME));
 IF :PARAMETER.P_CUSTOMER_ID IS NOT NULL THEN
 SET_BLOCK_PROPERTY('BK_CUSTOMER', DEFAULT_WHERE,
 'CUSTOMER_ID = ' || :PARAMETER.P_CUSTOMER_ID);
 END IF;
 GO_BLOCK('BK_CUSTOMER');
 EXECUTE_QUERY;
END;

Trigger.Name: WHEN-NEW-RECORD-INSTANCE
Trigger.TriggerText:
BEGIN
 -- Baseline for the POST-UPDATE audit trigger below: Forms has no
 -- built-in "old value" accessor, so the pre-change STATUS is stashed
 -- per record on entry (LOM-MOD-014).
 :GLOBAL.G_OLD_STATUS := :BK_CUSTOMER.STATUS;
END;

Trigger.Name: PRE-INSERT
Trigger.TriggerText:
BEGIN
 -- LOM-MOD-013 (CONVERT, category A): PK generated from a sequence in
 -- Forms' PRE-INSERT. Identical idiom repeated in ORDERS.fmb,
 -- INVENTORY.fmb is query-only so it does not need this. A straightforward
 -- mapping to an APEX page process / identity column; no business logic
 -- to lose.
 IF :BK_CUSTOMER.CUSTOMER_ID IS NULL THEN
 :BK_CUSTOMER.CUSTOMER_ID := lom_customer_id_seq.NEXTVAL;
 END IF;
 :BK_CUSTOMER.CREATED_BY := :GLOBAL.G_USER;
 :BK_CUSTOMER.CREATED_DATE := SYSDATE;
END;

Trigger.Name: POST-UPDATE
Trigger.TriggerText:
BEGIN
 -- LOM-MOD-014 (PRESERVE): unlike OM_SHARED.pll's log_action
 -- (LOM-MOD-039), this trigger calls LOM_AUDIT_API.log_event directly --
 -- already correctly centralized. Only the call site moves in APEX (a
 -- page process), the logic does not change.
 IF :BK_CUSTOMER.STATUS != :GLOBAL.G_OLD_STATUS THEN
 lom_audit_api.log_event(
 p_entity_name => 'CUSTOMER',
 p_entity_id => TO_CHAR(:BK_CUSTOMER.CUSTOMER_ID),
 p_action => 'STATUS_CHANGE',
 p_old_value => :GLOBAL.G_OLD_STATUS,
 p_new_value => :BK_CUSTOMER.STATUS,
 p_changed_by => :GLOBAL.G_USER
 );
 END IF;
 :GLOBAL.G_OLD_STATUS := :BK_CUSTOMER.STATUS;
END;

Trigger.Name: WHEN-VALIDATE-ITEM
Trigger.TriggerText:
DECLARE
 v_default_limit lom_customer_types.default_credit_limit%TYPE;
BEGIN
 SELECT default_credit_limit INTO v_default_limit
 FROM lom_customer_types
 WHERE customer_type_code = :BK_CUSTOMER.CUSTOMER_TYPE_CODE;

 -- LOM-MOD-012 (REPLACE_WITH_APEX_NATIVE, LOW risk): only a default
 -- suggestion, applied with COPY so it does not fire this item's own
 -- WHEN-VALIDATE-ITEM again and does not overwrite a value the user
 -- already typed. An APEX cascading LOV / page item default achieves the
 -- same UX with no PL/SQL.
 IF :BK_CUSTOMER.CREDIT_LIMIT IS NULL THEN
 COPY(TO_CHAR(v_default_limit), 'BK_CUSTOMER.CREDIT_LIMIT');
 END IF;
EXCEPTION
 WHEN NO_DATA_FOUND THEN
 NULL;
END;

Trigger.Name: WHEN-VALIDATE-ITEM
Trigger.TriggerText:
DECLARE
 v_open_orders NUMBER;
BEGIN
 IF :BK_CUSTOMER.STATUS = 'INACTIVE' AND :GLOBAL.G_OLD_STATUS = 'ACTIVE' THEN
 -- LOM-MOD-011 (MOVE_TO_PLSQL_API, HIGH risk): this duplicates
 -- LOM_CUSTOMER_API.has_open_orders, which LOM_CUSTOMER_API.change_status
 -- already calls before allowing the same transition. Two independent
 -- implementations of "does this customer have open orders" is exactly
 -- the kind of divergence risk this lab exists to surface: if one copy
 -- is fixed (e.g. the SHIPPED/REJECTED/CANCELLED exclusion list changes)
 -- and the other is not, the two layers silently disagree.
 SELECT COUNT(*) INTO v_open_orders
 FROM lom_orders
 WHERE customer_id = :BK_CUSTOMER.CUSTOMER_ID
 AND status NOT IN ('SHIPPED', 'REJECTED', 'CANCELLED');

 IF v_open_orders > 0 THEN
 om_shared.show_message('Cannot inactivate customer ' || :BK_CUSTOMER.CUSTOMER_ID
 || ': ' || v_open_orders || ' open order(s) still in progress.');
 RAISE FORM_TRIGGER_FAILURE;
 END IF;
 END IF;
END;

Trigger.Name: WHEN-VALIDATE-ITEM
Trigger.TriggerText:
BEGIN
 -- LOM-MOD-010 (MOVE_TO_PLSQL_API): duplicates CK_LOM_CUST_CREDIT
 -- (credit_limit >= 0). The DB constraint is the real guarantee; this
 -- trigger only exists to fail fast with a friendly message before
 -- COMMIT_FORM reaches the database.
 IF :BK_CUSTOMER.CREDIT_LIMIT < 0 THEN
 om_shared.show_message('Credit limit cannot be negative.');
 RAISE FORM_TRIGGER_FAILURE;
 END IF;
END;

Trigger.Name: WHEN-VALIDATE-ITEM
Trigger.TriggerText:
BEGIN
 -- LOM-MOD-015 (REPLACE_WITH_APEX_NATIVE, LOW risk): a hand-rolled shape
 -- check. APEX ships a native "Email" validation type; no PL/SQL needed.
 IF :BK_CUSTOMER.EMAIL IS NOT NULL
 AND NOT REGEXP_LIKE(:BK_CUSTOMER.EMAIL, '^[^@[:space:]]+@[^@[:space:]]+\.[^@[:space:]]+$') THEN
 om_shared.show_message('Email address does not look valid.');
 RAISE FORM_TRIGGER_FAILURE;
 END IF;
END;

RecordGroup.Name: RG_CUSTOMER_TYPE
RecordGroup.RecordGroupQuery: SELECT description, customer_type_code FROM lom_customer_types ORDER BY 1
